physical_mismatches.reason: The paper states that 3D stacking is future work. The model is 2.5D with compute dies and an I/O die on a passive interposer, so it cannot represent 3D heterogeneous integration or TSV/bonding thermal paths.

Interposer and package detail is incomplete. NoP power is assumed uniformly distributed over the interposer, and no interposer thickness, material or micro-bump/BEOL thermal parameters are given. Cooling parameters are taken from TESA [12] by reference only (convection resistance 0.4 K/W).

The workload is thermally static. HotSpot uses time-averaged component power from an analytical model (energy/delay), and the networks run sequentially. There is no transient thermal simulation and no workload-phase temperature trace, so the reported peak temperature is a steady-state estimate of average power.

The thermal-aware greedy mapping policy (high-power tasks on corner cores) and the TED+SCBO optimizer are not reproducible in a steady-state 2D Studio solve. Only a single fixed design with given power can be evaluated, not the DSE loop or mapping.

Per-block power values in W and block coordinates and sizes are not published for the selected design. Only totals are given: energy 59.8 mJ over 2.01 ms delay, and areas only as percentages in Fig. 10(a). Block-level power and geometry therefore cannot be reproduced from the packet.
No reliability or electromigration analysis is included; thermal constraints are limited to the peak-temperature bound.

studio_assumptions: Steady-state 2D conduction in the bundled Studio solver is used as an approximation of HotSpot 6.0 steady-state, with TIM, heat spreader and heat sink as lumped or layered package materials. Material properties are Studio defaults, since the paper only points to TESA [12] for values.
Ambient 45 C and convection resistance 0.4 K/W would be applied as the paper's stated boundary conditions only if a complete floorplan and power set were available.

No floorplan or power rows are provided in this extraction because block geometry and per-block watts are missing. Total chip power is not split among blocks without a published rule, and dimensions or powers from other scenarios (e.g., B1-B4, the 200 mm2 case) are not mixed in.
